item.title: Immediate large-scale cortical network changes following acupuncture in patients with disorders of consciousness: a resting-state fNIRS study
item.description: Introduction Disorders of consciousness (DOC) involve severe disruption of large-scale brain networks. This study investigated immediate cortical network changes following acupuncture in patients with DOC using functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS).

item.title: Electroencephalography as a biomarker of brain function in domestic ruminants: a systematic review and critical appraisal
item.description: BACKGROUND: Electroencephalography (EEG) has been extensively used to investigate cortical activity in ruminants under physiological, pathological, and experimental conditions. Its applications range from the assessment of consciousness and nociception to experimental models of hypoxia-ischemia, neurodevelopment, pain, anesthesia, and neurological disorders.

item.title: A longitudinal analysis of the clinical practice of ketamine assisted psychotherapy with adolescents and young adults
item.description: Introduction Ketamine Assisted Psychotherapy (KAP) is a developing modality with broad impact on humans suffering with a variety of emotional and relationship difficulties that encompass many diagnostic entities. Our application of KAP has extended to and included the treatment of adolescents and young adults in a family therapy format.

item.title: Emergent flow theory: autonomic coherence as a gain parameter for the temporal architecture of conscious integration
item.description: Contemporary neuroscientific theories of consciousness—including Global Neuronal Workspace Theory (GNW), Integrated Information Theory (IIT), and the Predictive Processing/Free Energy Principle (PP/FEP)—have not formalized autonomic and neuromodulatory state as explicit dynamic control parameters within models of conscious integration. This gap constitutes the explanatory niche addressed by the Emergent Flow Theory (EFT).

item.title: The Thermodynamic and Recursive Architecture of Universal Modular Dynamics: From Meta-Law Fixed Points to Emergent Spacetime, Particle Hierarchies, and Non-Geometric Phase Transitions
item.description: We develop a comprehensive, mathematically closed, and self-consistent formal framework for Universal Modular Dynamics (UMD), establishing a paradigm shift wherein physical reality emerges as a stable, recursive fixed-point projection (Ω⋆ = H(Ω⋆)) of higher-order meta-law dynamics driven by a meta-time parameter (T) operating on a pre-physical possibility space. Rather than treating spacetime, quantum fields, or cosmological constants as fundamental primitives, we derive the continuous Riemannian spacetime metric…

item.title: A multimodal investigation of altered cortical metabolism in patients with disorders of consciousness
item.description: Disorders of consciousness (DoC) are characterised by marked reductions in cerebral glucose metabolism, but the specific cellular and neurochemical processes driving this impairment remain unclear. To elucidate these mechanisms, a multimodal imaging approach combining [18F]-fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography (FDG-PET) and magnetic resonance spectroscopy (MRS) was applied to the posterior medial cortex (PMC) in 15 DoC patients and 14 healthy controls.

item.title: Hitting and missing on consciousness
item.description: Disturbances of conscious experience are central features of many psychiatric and mental health disorders. Experimental studies of conscious perception are therefore increasingly cited in clinical and translational work under the assumption that they identify neural mechanisms specific to subjective experience.

item.title: Multimodal biomarkers of response to transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation in disorders of consciousness: a study protocol
item.description: Patients with disorders of consciousness (DOC) have limited options for arousal-promoting interventions. Transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation (taVNS), a non-invasive neuromodulation technique, has shown potential to improve conscious behaviors in a subset of patients with DOC.

item.title: Neurophysiological signatures of latent brain vulnerability in perioperative neurocognitive disorders: integrating EEG, cerebral oximetry, and processed EEG
item.description: Perioperative neurocognitive disorders (PND) remain difficult to prevent because conventional cognitive assessments may fail to capture brain vulnerability in patients who appear cognitively normal before anesthesia and surgery. This narrative review examines the potential role of objective perioperative neuromonitoring markers as complements to cognitive scales, focusing on electroencephalography (EEG), near-infrared spectroscopy (NIRS)/cerebral oximetry, and processed EEG/bispectral index (BIS).

item.title: Progress of nursing management for delirium in critically ill geriatric patients: a narrative review
item.description: Delirium is the most common and modifiable acute cognitive complication in elderly critically ill patients and is associated with prolonged hospital stays, increased mortality, persistent long-term cognitive decline, and a significant healthcare burden. A history of mild cognitive impairment or dementia further increases delirium risk, exacerbates symptom severity, and worsens clinical outcomes.

item.title: Topological integration and segregation of the conscious connectome as biomarkers for state, behavior, and prognosis
item.description: Consciousness is hypothesized to emerge from a sophisticated balance between functional integration and segregation across large-scale brain networks. However, how these topological properties are disrupted in disorders of consciousness (DoC), and whether they can predict long-term recovery, remain to be established.

item.title: Acute psilocybin or ethocybin leads to a sustained increase in Pavlovian aversion memory in male mice
item.description: There is considerable interest in the concept that psychedelic compounds might facilitate reorganization of emotional processing with therapeutic benefit; in particular, amelioration of excessive focus on past, current and potential-future aversive events, a dominant emotional-cognitive state in stress-related affective disorders. Translational animal models can advance understanding of specific aspects of this concept, namely, those relating to subconscious emotional memories and their neurobiology.
